column3: NASB reads “But,” as other manuscripts do; the critical text has “For.” It adds “for my own sake” and renders “grief” as “sorrow.”
NASB follows the critical text; “grief” is rendered “sorrow,” and it adds “would be the joy of.”
NASB renders “more abundantly” as “especially” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “that I may not burden” as “in order not to say too much” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “that I may know the proof of you” as “that I might put you to the test.”
NASB follows the critical text (“what”); it adds “I did it” and renders “for you” as “for your sakes.”
NASB renders “be outwitted” as “no advantage be taken of us.”
NASB renders “in the spirit” as “for my spirit” and “went out” as “went on.”
NASB renders “leading in triumph” as “leads us in His triumph” and “fragrance” as “sweet aroma.”
NASB renders “a sweet perfume” as “a fragrance.”
NASB follows the critical text (“from … to”); “sufficient” is rendered “adequate.”
NASB follows the critical text (“in the sight of God”); “the many” is rendered “many.”
